diameter_m.source: Rules of Golf, Definitions: Hole, 4 1/4 in across

depth_m.source: Rules of Golf, Definitions: Hole, at least 4 in deep

max_speed_mps.source: Penner (2002), 'The physics of putting', Can. J. Phys. 80:83-96, fitting Holmes (1991), Am. J. Phys. 59:129-136: dead centre, counting capture helped by the far rim

free_fall_max_speed_mps.source: Penner (2002): dead centre, falling a ball radius before the far wall

capture.off_centre: Penner (2002): captured below max_speed * (1 - (offset / hole radius)^2)
capture.rim_roll_studies: Hubbard & Smith (1999), 'Dynamics of golf ball-hole interactions: rolling around the rim', J. Dyn. Sys. Meas. Control 121:88-95: the capture boundary falls as the ball arrives off centre
capture.lip_outs: fast or off-centre balls ride the rim and spin out

diameter_m.source: Tom Mase (2019), Take the Flagstick Out!, Golf Digest: tested sticks approximately half an inch in diameter at green level

maximum_diameter_m.source: Rules of Equipment, Part 8 (Committee equipment): at most 0.75 in (19 mm) from 3 in above to 3 in below the putting surface

pelz.source: Dave Pelz (2019-01-02), The science proves you should leave the flagstick in when you putt
pelz.finding: A fibreglass flagstick absorbs energy from the ball, giving gravity longer to pull it into the cup.

mase.source: Tom Mase (2019-03-28), Take the Flagstick Out!
mase.finding: At 2.5 feet past, direct and off-centre hits dropped with or without the pin. At 4.5 feet past, some off-centre hits were rejected. Direct hits at 9 to 12 feet past mostly dropped with fibreglass pins when they missed with the pin out.

mygolfspy.source: MyGolfSpy (2019-01-16), TESTED: Flagstick In (vs) Flagstick Out?
mygolfspy.finding: Machine tests used two pin rigidities and direct and off-centre strikes. A more compliant pin helped direct hits by losing more speed. Firm glancing hits could still miss.

simulation_checks.note: The experiments report roll-past distances, not entry speeds in m/s or one universal rejection speed. Tests derive speeds for this flat test green from rolling_deceleration; the source greens and exact make percentages are not reproduced. The contact restitution is a simulation fit, not a reported material measurement.

leniency.source: golf++ design: the one named departure from the real cup (cup_leniency)
